vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 30. Nay or No: 10. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 39 (98%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 51 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

posts.text: On Veterans Day, we honor the brave men and women who have served our country and recognize the sacrifices they have made to defend our freedoms. It is because of their courage that we are able to enjoy our freedoms in the greatest country in the world. We are forever grateful https://t.co/bJhHxke9O1

Congratulations to my friend @LeaderJohnThune on his reelection as Senate Republican leader. John is a trusted colleague and a steady voice, which has served our group well over the past two years as we’ve worked to advance our Republican agenda, and will continue to do so.

Good to see Rick Williamson and Rick Vanden Hoek with the VFW Department of South Dakota in DC this week. Grateful for their continued advocacy on behalf of our nation’s veterans, especially as we recognize Veterans Day this week. https://t.co/DHu0mUI6Fx

While I appreciate my Senate colleagues opening a much-needed conversation surrounding permitting reform, I voted against the motion to proceed on H.R.2347 tonight. I believe any discussions surrounding permitting reform should allow for the opportunity to resolve any issues at the state level.
In South Dakota, the siting of most transmission lines has always been resolved in a reasonable amount of time between landowners, developers and the Public Utilities Commission. This legislation would transfer contested cases to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission if not resolved within 12 months, giving a weighted advantage to the developer. South Dakota landowners deserve to negotiate with stakeholders at the state and local level before federal intervention is required.
I hope to continue to work with my colleagues to address this concern.

Good to meet with Mitchell and Carter from Aberdeen Central High School to hear about their experience at the America’s Youth AI Festival, where they joined students from all 50 states to develop the nation’s first student-led AI policy for K-12 schools. Their work on the https://t.co/8fmuQyOyVZ
Good conversation at the 2026 South Dakota Biotech Summit in Sioux Falls where we discussed South Dakota’s role in America’s innovation future. https://t.co/SS8B9Vmy52

On this day in 1889, South Dakota became a state. 137 years later, it’s the greatest place in the world to live, work and raise a family, all thanks to the many people who call our state home. Happy Birthday, South Dakota! https://t.co/TV6jvg5LO9
Praying for a fast and full recovery for my colleague Chris. https://t.co/qnr1KuOnPF
Always fun to have grandkids and friends come by to trick or treat! Happy Halloween! https://t.co/iUmjfnhRiz
Good to have some of the family together this weekend, including 8 of my siblings! Great way to spend my birthday. https://t.co/msjQ6gB1Fb

As our nation faces increasingly complex national security threats, we must make certain the Air Force Academy has the resources, facilities and training necessary to develop the next generation of military leaders. My colleagues and I on the USAFA Board of Visitors recently sent our semiannual report to the Department of War. This report makes recommendations for the Academy, including modernizing cadet training, strengthening infrastructure and preparing future Air and Space Force officers for modern warfare. Read more here:
https://t.co/6VyV1NRLDn
Appreciated meeting with leadership from the South Dakota State Medical Association in Sioux Falls this week. https://t.co/rsuqCvMfjm

Good to be in attendance for today’s groundbreaking on the new Platte-Winner bridge. I am pleased that we were able to secure $25 million for this project as part of the appropriations process for FY26. This new bridge, which replaces the original built in 1966, is estimated to https://t.co/xEqIiwPmI1

Visited Sioux Falls Christian High School today to speak with AP Government students. Appreciated their thoughtful questions about public service, including making South Dakota better for the next generation. The future is bright! Thank you to Mr. Hilbrands for the invitation. https://t.co/EUnyTgU2E4
Photos of granddaughter Elaina on her first hunt with me in Pre-K and today’s hunt. Hard to believe she’ll graduate high school this year! https://t.co/ixSq8qZlsR
Another successful pheasant opener. Ready for a great season! https://t.co/7bX4AOPLOi
Today’s the day! Pheasant season is here, and South Dakotans across the state are taking to the field with family and friends. Wishing everyone a safe and successful hunt! https://t.co/RmIBbu3nRJ

Today, my Sioux Falls office received a suspicious piece of mail. My team members followed proper protocols advised by U.S. Capitol Police and contacted the Sioux Falls Police Department, who responded immediately to investigate and evacuate the office.
 
I am grateful for the U.S. Capitol Police, who intercepted other letters and sent out a warning allowing my team to recognize this letter before opening it, and to the Sioux Falls Police Department. I am also grateful for all of my team members, who work tirelessly on behalf of South Dakotans despite the risks involved. Our Sioux Falls office will be closed for the remainder of the day as SFPD continues to investigate and will reopen for normal hours on Monday morning.
 
This situation is deeply concerning and follows a trend of intimidating tactics that impact our team members. This has no place in our nation. America is better than this.

Saddened to hear of the passing of Deputy Katherine Frank. My prayers are with her family, friends and fellow officers as they grieve this loss. We must never forget the sacrifices made by those who protect and serve our communities. https://t.co/MVllWxVYhE

Today, on Native Americans’ Day we honor the rich history, culture and traditions of Native American communities and recognize their lasting impact on South Dakota and our nation. #NativeAmericansDay https://t.co/oF18mLHrwK

Please join me in praying for the officer in critical condition, her loved ones and the entire Minnehaha County Sheriff’s Office following this tragic incident. Today and every day, we support our law enforcement officers who work tirelessly to keep our communities safe. https://t.co/VZC3p83TWH

Following my letter last week, I’m pleased to see that the President is taking steps to lower fuel prices, including a review of certain taxes on diesel. This is an opportunity to offer real relief to South Dakotans who continue to pay higher prices at the pump, particularly farmers and ranchers who are in the middle of harvest. We’ll continue to work on addressing the high cost of living impacting our state.

Glad to sit down last week with Coleen Globke Brasch, my 2027 Angels in Adoption honoree and founder and executive director of All About U Adoptions, headquartered in Sioux Falls.

Coleen is an inspiring example of someone who leads with compassion and cares deeply for everyone involved in the adoption process. It was a pleasure to visit with her, hear more about her story and learn about the meaningful work she is doing through All About U Adoptions.

Spoke with Mark from Renner and Anna from Sioux Falls, who are members of the Senior Care Pharmacy Coalition, about the importance of keeping pharmacies at long-term care facilities open and available for South Dakotans. https://t.co/u1AhB9eglB
Great to visit with Austin from Dakota State University, representing the Computing Research Association, to talk about issues relating to his field of study. https://t.co/QKNtw5nSXW

Good to see Dr. Jami Jo Thompson, Superintendent of Rapid City Area Schools. Appreciated our conversation on the importance of funding public education in South Dakota and placing control at the local level. https://t.co/4Q1mj5aRWh

It was a privilege to sit down with South Dakotan Kate Utley, whose husband lost his life while serving our nation in 2012, and other Gold Star families. Appreciated this group taking the time to share stories of their loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice in defense of America. We are grateful for their service.

Good to visit with South Dakota folks representing Impact Aid schools in our state. These funds are crucial for the success of schools located near large sections of federally-owned land, and I’ll continue to advocate for fully funding this program in the Senate. https://t.co/Pw8KaVZRSp

Met with a few South Dakota folks with Growth Energy to talk about the need for year-round access to E15. We all appreciated the Senate Ag Committee advancing a Farm Bill that included a provision to allow for year-round access to E15. https://t.co/bkWf3Toflr
Had a good conversation with Lisa from Keystone and Linda from Leola with Concerned Women for America. Enjoyed discussing issues important to South Dakotans. https://t.co/2D1tSmQfa6

Today I voted in favor of the Ratepayer Protection Act to protect families and small businesses from paying higher electric bills due to data center construction in their communities. The key to this bill is preserving state local control. Data centers should only be built if their companies pay their own way and provide the power they consume. Very pleased that South Dakota is leading the way with similar legislation already in place at the state level.

Good to see Adam Bode, CEO of DemKota Ranch Beef in Aberdeen, in DC recently. Appreciated hearing about their efforts to distribute locally sourced, high-quality American beef. https://t.co/C40iFrsVzO
Recently sat down with South Dakotans representing the turkey industry to discuss animal health, ag labor and trade priorities. https://t.co/76zkHYYQyx
Always enjoy visiting with South Dakota Pork Producers about their work delivering quality pork products in South Dakota and beyond. https://t.co/aTWH9iqxK3
Good to meet with the Dakota Credit Union Association to discuss ways Congress can support credit unions and the South Dakotans they serve. https://t.co/ve28lqOVLF

South Dakota is the top producer of bison in the country. South Dakota producers with the National Bison Association shared that demand is at an all time high. They’re focused on bison herd health as well as making sure we have enough grazing land for livestock to meet that demand. We talked about my legislation, the RANCH Act, which would increase the amount of grazing land available for livestock.
Sat down with South Dakota Autodealers Association to discuss federal policies impacting autodealers across the state. https://t.co/8BS7PMwDSc
South Dakotans with American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network came by recently to talk about the importance of cancer research funding at the federal level. https://t.co/Dirsy5upN4
Enjoyed meeting with Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe Chairman Ryman LeBeau and CRST leadership for an update on the new school in Eagle Butte, which recently broke ground. https://t.co/uijC1LnAZ9

Good to sit down with Scott Landguth of the South Dakota Ellsworth Development Authority and Bob Taylor to talk about the activity at Ellsworth Air Force Base in preparation for the B-21. It’s been a team effort to prepare the necessary infrastructure for this new program and all the airmen it brings. We’re ready for the arrival of the first B-21 Raider bombers next year.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
